environment.description: Same application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB with the following configuration: ALB idle timeout set to 4s with HTTP/2 multiplexing enabled across variable-latency target group instances (3 tasks, min). pgBouncer configured in statement pooling mode with server_lifetime=120 and server_idle_timeout=30, causing connection reassignment between every statement execution. ECS task networking uses awsvpc mode with a security group that restricts /internal/* path access via ALB listener rule priority 1 (fixed-response 403 for any request matching path-pattern '/internal/*' from non-VPC sources). Additionally, the ALB has a custom response-time bucketing behavior: the ALB access logs show that the 'target_processing_time' field exhibits ±15ms jitter due to Fargate's shared-tenancy vCPU credit scheduling combined with pgBouncer's statement-mode connection acquisition latency variance (measured p50=8ms, p99=47ms for connection checkout). This infrastructure-induced timing noise exceeds the signal delta of the byte-by-byte string comparison (~2-5ns per character difference), making statistical timing attacks infeasible even with thousands of samples.

config.compute: ECS Fargate, 3 tasks minimum, shared-tenancy vCPU

alb_listener_rules.action: fixed-response 403 unless source from VPC CIDR 10.0.0.0/16

config.network_security_group: restrict /internal/* to VPC CIDR only via ALB rule
